_comment: Federal wave F7 decision record, and the wave's own artifact: written by hand, read by scripts/vr-gen-federal-wave-f7-migration.mjs and checked by scripts/test-vr-federal-wave-f7.mjs. Every refusal in this file is an argument against a written scope note or a standing rule, never against a feeling about a measure. Where this wave departs from a face the corpus already ships, the departure is labelled as one and the reason is stated -- there is exactly one, foreign_balance.
mission: Formal pattern density from the 113 rolls F6 left unread: the Senate slice first, then the District of Columbia measures keyed on their subjects. Ingest and map in one pass. No party score, no package percentage, no invented stance, no floor moved. Stance harvest and direct messages are out of scope.

whatShipsThisWave.note: Nineteen measures and nineteen roll calls: fourteen Senate war-powers resolutions on three texts, four District of Columbia bills on their own subjects, and one House amendment repealing two authorizations for the use of military force. Twenty-eight mapping rows on six keys that were already live and already placed -- restraint, war_powers, strong_defense, border_security, deportations, tough_on_crime. Seven of the fourteen Senate rolls ship with zero mapping rows on purpose; censusRule34 is the argument and the member-for-member diff. CACHE_VERSION moves because consistency.js gains _DOS_MECH pairs for the judged acts.

censusRule34.rule: db/vr-ingest-runbook.md rule 34: the same text voted twice is two acts; admit both when each is the only record of somebody's position, and state in the file what the second does NOT add -- the member-for-member diff, not a claim.
censusRule34.whyItGovernsThisWave: Twelve of the fourteen Senate rolls are two texts, not twelve. Eleven are the Iran withdrawal resolution with a different sponsor on the cover and identical operative language; two are the Venezuela resolution. Mapping all fourteen would have handed every senator eleven judged acts on restraint for one position held once, which is manufactured density -- the opposite of what this wave was asked to measure.
censusRule34.test: For each text, in vote-date order, count the (member, position) pairs a roll records that no earlier roll on the same text records, counting only yea and nay. A not_voting is not a judged act and contributes no position, so it cannot earn a mapping.

questionC_theNineDistrictMeasures.method: Read the engrossed text or the CRS summary of each, then test the subject against the written scope in issue-scope.js. Venue was never a candidate: F6 already ran the six vocab rules on a District key and refused it, and rule 5 -- subject not vehicle -- is the rule it failed.

refusedDetail.subject: police discipline, use-of-force and vehicular pursuit rules for the Metropolitan Police Department
refusedDetail.why: Refused for want of a directional key, and every candidate was tested in writing. tough_on_crime's OUT list sends away 'funding and backing law enforcement itself (Back Law Enforcement), the accountability pairing' -- these measures are the accountability pairing. back_police has no written scope note and its shipped pattern is money plus offences against officers; these bills carry neither. justice_reform has no written scope note either. justice_balance is a _balance key, permanently unread by _rdSuppressedKey(), and F6's shipped wall forbids parking a row there. The vocabulary gap is named in vocabDecision rather than papered over, and the three measures stay unread.
refusedDetail.whatWouldReopenThem: A police-accountability key that passes all six vocab rules, with a written scope note and a pole. This wave did not write one and says so.

refusedDetail.subject: an advisory commission and a cleanliness programme for the District
refusedDetail.why: Two refusals, either of which is sufficient. The runbook's study-and-report rule: an institution that studies and reports is not a policy vote, and the commission limb is exactly that -- F6 applied the same rule to four federal energy bills. The cleanliness programme limb has no subject key at all, and what is left after both is 'it happened in the District', which is venue. Rule 5 already refused venue.

refusedDetail.why: The honest key is checks_balances, and runbook rule 28 says checks_balances takes no roll-call mappings. No second key was reached for. Refused on the standing rule, named here so the next wave does not re-derive it.

questionD_theAmendmentRolls.question: House amendment rolls F6 could not list under the parent bill number -- can the amendment text and a contested question be identified?
questionD_theAmendmentRolls.whyF6CouldNotListThem: The House files an amendment roll under its parent bill's number, so a menu listing shows the parent and never the amendment. F6 named 89 of them as unreachable without a per-roll pass.
questionD_theAmendmentRolls.theBridge: For each amendment roll, fetch the PARENT bill's BILLSTATUS and read its <amendments> collection, matching on the roll number inside each amendment's own action text. That gives the H.Amdt. number, the sponsor and the purpose from the amendment's own record.
questionD_theAmendmentRolls.aBugWorthRecording: The first bridge run reported 0 unique matches and 88 ambiguous. 'Roll no. NNN' occurs twice inside every <amendment> block -- once in <latestAction><text> and once in <links><name> -- so each amendment collided with itself. De-duplicating the roll numbers per block fixed it. This is the same duplication class that makes a first-match regex on <latestAction> attribute one measure's roll number to another, which is why every roll in this wave was verified against its own per-roll LIS or clerk document rather than against a BILLSTATUS listing.

onSubjectScope.subject: joint resolutions of disapproval under section 36 of the Arms Export Control Act, on proposed foreign military sales to Qatar and to the United Arab Emirates
onSubjectScope.why: Contested, in form, never refused before, and still not mappable -- which is worth saying plainly because it is a vocabulary gap and not a judgment about the vote. Filing these on israel_support because they are arms sales in the same region would be the adjacency reasoning rule 41 forbids. They stay unread, and the gap is named in vocabDecision.

vocabDecision.whyThatIsTheRightOutcome: The brief allows a key when all six rules pass and requires it to be placed on the topic tree the same pass. Writing a key whose boundary cannot be stated is how gov_regulation became a dumping ground, and F6's wall against restuffing it is the same wall seen from the other side.

measures.documentTitle: A joint resolution to direct the removal of United States Armed Forces from hostilities that have not been authorized by Congress.
measures.purpose: Directs the President to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities that have not been authorized by Congress unless a declaration of war or a specific authorization for the use of military force has been enacted.
measures.question: On the Motion to Discharge S.J.Res. 83
measures.decisiveWhy: A war-powers resolution under 50 U.S.C. 1544(c) reaches the floor only if the Foreign Relations Committee is discharged, so the discharge motion IS the vote on the resolution: a rejected motion ends the measure and no vote on passage ever occurs. This is the same admitted form F4 used for the arms-sale disapprovals.
measures.rule11: cleared -- the losing side holds 48.5% of the yea+nay pool, far above the one-tenth bar

issues.rationale: The resolution's operative section directs the President to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities that Congress has not authorized, and its saving clause preserves only defence against an attack already under way or imminent. The instrument's whole command is withdrawal, so the direction on the key is not inferred from a title: a yea ordered forces out and a nay left them in. This is the face S.J.Res. 59 already carries for the identical form and the identical question -- restraint w100 primary yea_supports, war_powers w70, strong_defense w55 opposed -- and it is copied rather than re-derived, because runbook rule 25 says the same subject may not be mapped two ways without a written reason and there is no reason here: this is the same subject.

A privileged joint resolution under section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, which reached the floor only because the Foreign Relations Committee was discharged, and what it asserts is that the decision to authorize belongs to Congress. war_powers sits in _RD_NO_POLE in stance-helpers.js, so this row is inventory and never prints a direction: it records that the member voted on a war-powers instrument, which is true, and it makes no claim about where they stand. Filed at 70 rather than 100 because the operative command is the removal of forces rather than a change to the authorization machinery itself -- the weight S.J.Res. 59 carries for the same reason.

A yea withdraws United States forces from an ongoing engagement absent a vote of Congress, and that is what strong_defense reads as its opposed direction. The weight is held at 55, the weight S.J.Res. 59 carries, because the resolution takes no position on force levels, procurement, budgets or posture; it reaches one engagement and stops. Recording it lower would erase a real vote and recording it higher would turn a single-engagement question into a defence-posture score.

declinedKeys.why: A WRITTEN DEPARTURE from the precedent face, and the only one. S.J.Res. 59 carries foreign_balance w45 from the July 2026 landmark pass with the rationale 'Concerns the scope and restraint of U.S. military involvement abroad.' F7 does not copy it. _rdSuppressedKey() in stance-helpers.js returns 'balance_key' for any key ending in _balance, which means such a row is permanently unread: it can never print a direction and never counts toward a characterised reading. F6's shipped wall was 'no *_balance key was used to park anything', and seven more measures times one unread row is exactly the parking F6 forbade. Dropping it changes no reader-visible sentence, because the row it would create is one the reader never sees. The three rows that ship carry the whole of what the vote says.

Refused because the repository already removed it from this instrument by hand. Migration 20260904000000_vr_split_umbrella_issue_keys.sql re-keyed S.J.Res. 59's america_first_fp w70 to war_powers, and its own comment names the five war-powers instruments it moved. Adding the umbrella key back on a fresh measure of the same form would undo a settled re-key from outside it, which runbook rule 21 exists to prevent.

Not adjacent, not applicable, and named because the corpus's other Middle East instruments carry it. None of these resolutions mentions Israel, and the Iran ones reach only United States forces in hostilities with Iran. Runbook rule 41: a cousin refusal is settled on the shipped scope note, never on the fact that two subjects share a region.

measures.shortTitle: District of Columbia Federal Immigration Compliance Act of 2025
measures.officialTitle: To require the District of Columbia to comply with federal immigration laws.
measures.purpose: Bars the District from adopting any law, policy or practice that limits its cooperation with federal immigration enforcement, including the exchange of citizenship or immigration status information and compliance with lawful detainer and release-notification requests, with a carve-out for witnesses and victims of crime.

issues.rationale: The Act's whole mechanism is the state and local end of federal immigration enforcement: it forbids the District from adopting a law, policy or practice that stops its entities from sending, receiving, maintaining or exchanging citizenship or immigration status information, and from declining lawful federal requests. border_security's written scope in issue-scope.js names, as what is IN, 'the state and local cooperation that feeds the federal system' -- this Act is that clause and almost nothing else. Weight 75 rather than 100 because the key's scope also covers the physical border and the entry apparatus, which this Act does not touch, and because the carve-out for witnesses and victims of crime is a real limit on the mandate rather than a recital. A yea compelled the cooperation.

The second operative limb reaches detainers and release notification -- the District may not decline a lawful request to hold or to notify before release -- and that is the hand-off by which a person in local custody enters removal proceedings. deportations' written scope names 'mandatory custody and removal -- who the executive must detain and place in removal proceedings'. This Act does not itself order a removal, which is why it is filed at 70 and secondary: it removes the local discretion that currently interrupts the chain. The CRS summary confirms the clause; the engrossed text was read for it rather than the summary alone.

declinedKeys.why: Refused on the key's own OUT list, which names 'immigration detention and removal' in terms. The measure creates no offence, changes no offence level and alters no sentence, so nothing in tough_on_crime's IN enumeration -- offence elements, offence levels, mandatory minimums, sentencing enhancements, juvenile adjustment and expungement -- is engaged. That the bill is about custody is not enough: the OUT line was written for exactly this confusion.

The Act does constrain what the District's own government may enact, and that is a federal-local authority question. Runbook rule 28: checks_balances takes no roll-call mappings. Named rather than silently dropped, because it is the honest second reading of the measure and the reason it is not filed is a standing rule, not an absence.
Refused as restuffing. F6's shipped wall forbids using gov_regulation as a home for anything that has a subject key, and this measure has two.

measures.decisiveWhy: The amendment's own text is the whole question — it repeals two standing authorizations for the use of military force — and the amendment was disposed of by recorded vote on its own, not en bloc. The parent bill's passage roll is a separate act on a separate subject.
measures.parentTitle: Streamlining Procurement for Effective Execution and Delivery and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026

issues.rationale: The amendment's text is the whole question and the question is the authorization itself: it repeals the 2002 authorization for the use of military force against Iraq and the 1991 authorization. war_powers is the subject of who may authorize the use of force and on what standing grant, and this instrument changes that machinery directly rather than ordering any force to move -- so the weight is 100 and the row is primary. war_powers sits in _RD_NO_POLE in stance-helpers.js, so the row is inventory: the reader is told the member voted on a war-powers instrument and is told nothing about a direction, which is the correct outcome for a repeal of superseded standing authority.

Filed at 70 and secondary, which is the mirror of the face the war-powers resolutions in this same wave carry, and rule 25 requires the reason for the difference to be written down. The resolutions order forces out of an engagement now under way; their operative subject is the scope of American military involvement, so restraint leads there at 100. This amendment moves no forces and ends no engagement -- it withdraws two standing legal authorizations. The restraint reading is real, because a repealed authorization is one fewer basis for future action, but it is a consequence of the change rather than the change, and 70 is where a consequence is recorded.

declinedKeys.why: Refused, and the argument matters because the war-powers resolutions in this same wave DO carry strong_defense at 55 opposed. The reason those carry it is stated in S.J.Res. 59's own shipped rationale: 'A yea withdraws U.S. forces from an ongoing engagement absent a vote of Congress.' That sentence is false of this amendment. Nothing is withdrawn from anywhere; two authorizations that no operation now relies on are struck from the books, and the amendment carried 261-167 with support from both sides of the chamber. Copying the row because the words look alike would be the adjacency reasoning rule 41 forbids, and it would publish an opposed direction on a defence key for 261 members on no evidence.
Same written departure as on the fourteen resolutions: a _balance key is permanently unread by _rdSuppressedKey(), and F6's wall forbids parking a row there.

attribution.rule: Fail-closed, and the two chambers take different paths because the two sources carry different identifiers.
attribution.housePath: bioguide from the clerk's own name-id attribute, then db/vr-member-map.json. A recorded member who does not resolve is skipped and counted.
attribution.senatePath: There is no bioguide in the LIS XML, so the only available key is (surname, state) resolved against the roster with a whole-name compare, plus the LIS member id where present. A surname that resolves to more than one distinct person in the same state is skipped and counted as ambiguous, never guessed. Ambiguous skips this wave: 0.
attribution.totalsAreFullChamber: yea, nay, present and notVoting come from <count><yeas>/<nays> in the Senate document and <totals-by-vote> in the clerk's, and they count every recorded member. The attributed rows are a smaller set and the two live in separate fields. There is a specific trap here: the LIS <vote_tally> element renders '51-42' as a display string, which parses to 5142 and makes the losing side zero, so rule 11 would pass everything. The authority is the count block.

ceiling.note: The roster holds 221 slugs, 99 of them senators. Every Senate roll here records all 100 senators, so the ceiling is a roster question and not a reading question: three serving senators are absent from db/vr-member-map.json -- Husted (OH) and Hyde-Smith (MS) on all fourteen rolls, and Armstrong (OK) on the nine rolls after Mullin left. That is 37 unattributable rows. They are named rather than fixed, because adding a roster slug is a roster wave with its own argument and this wave was asked for ingest and mapping.

attribution.rollToMeasureVerification: Every roll's measure was read off the roll's OWN document -- <document_type> and <document_number> in the Senate XML, <legis-num> in the clerk's -- and asserted against the seed. This is not defensive habit: govinfo repeats <latestAction> once per related bill and amendment, so a first-match regex made S.J.Res. 98 claim roll 608 and made four identical-text Iran resolutions each claim roll 46. Clerk punctuation also differs from corpus punctuation ('H R 2056' against 'H.R. 2056'), so the comparison is on alphanumerics only.

readDisclosure.note: Nothing is promoted and nothing is retracted, so no existing row's reading changes and the no-loss check has no promote to check. Every mapping row is new, on a measure that was not on file. The measured before and after counts are below, on the rule 36 method: the row model's own read flag over every pid, set-wise, never a shape counter that can net a lost reading against a gained one.
readDisclosure.primaryWallChecked: Runbook rule 30 says to check the primary wall BEFORE shipping a depth pass, and the count first: of the twenty-eight rows TWELVE are primary and sixteen are secondary — seven restraint primaries on the Senate rolls, one war_powers primary on the amendment, one border_security primary and three tough_on_crime primaries on the District bills. FOUR of the six keys gain a primary from this wave. TWO DO NOT, and saying otherwise would be the easy false sentence here: deportations gains exactly one secondary row (H.R. 2056, where the border_security row is the primary), and strong_defense gains seven secondary rows and no primary at all, because a resolution ordering forces out of one engagement is not a vote on force levels, procurement or posture. WHAT THAT ACTUALLY COSTS, read in the shipped code rather than assumed. _RD_MIN_PRIMARY is no longer a lock on characterisation: stance-helpers.js:1573 records that the last primary gate was removed on purpose ('isPrimary is a label on the bill, printable everywhere and consultable by nothing'), and the surviving use at stance-helpers.js:1598 only decides whether _rdPackageNote's sentence prints beside the finding. So a secondary-only key cannot suppress or downgrade a reading; the exposure is that a member whose whole reading on such a key rests on non-primary acts is told so in a sentence. MEASURED, not argued: of the 98 members this wave touches on strong_defense and the 116 it touches on deportations, the number who become newly readable on those keys is 0 and the number whose reading starts printing the package sentence is 0 — every one of them already held at least one primary act on the key from an earlier instrument. The wall is clear on the numbers, not on the structure, and it is stated that way. The one place the sentence WOULD be true if it ever printed is worth recording as well: a withdrawal resolution genuinely is mainly about something other than defence posture, which is exactly why the strong_defense row is filed at 55 and secondary, so _rdPackageNote would be telling the reader something accurate rather than papering over a mis-keyed row.
readDisclosure.floorsUntouched: _RD_MIN_PRIMARY, _RD_MIN_JUDGED, _RD_THIN_MIN, _RD_MIN_STRENGTH, _RD_DOMINANCE, _RD_SPLIT_MIN_JUDGED, _RD_SPLIT_MIN_SIDE, _PDX_RD_MEMBER_FLOOR and the publication floor are neither read nor written by this wave.
readDisclosure.noPoleKeysDoNotPrintADirection: war_powers is in _RD_NO_POLE in stance-helpers.js, so _rdSuppressedKey() returns 'no_pole' for it and its rows keep inventory copy and never print a stance. Eight of the twenty-eight rows are war_powers rows (seven discharge motions plus the NDAA amendment), so twenty rows print a direction and eight do not; the seed says so plainly rather than letting a reader assume twenty-eight new directional readings.

theMeasurementDefectFoundWhileWritingThi.what: The first draft of this disclosure published EIGHT rows as having changed direction. The measured figure is FIFTEEN. The eight was not a typo and not a second definition of the word: scripts/vr-federal-fpi.mjs built its per-issue tier list only over the pids whose SHAPE COUNTERS had moved, and a member who loses a direction on one key while gaining one on another nets out to identical counters and never enters that list at all.
theMeasurementDefectFoundWhileWritingThi.theMemberWhoExposedIt: angus_king. His strong_defense fell from Mostly supports to Split on seven war-powers yeas, and his restraint rose from Split to Mostly supports on the same seven, so his shape came out identical on both sides -- readable, 67 issues, 7 clear, 13 split, 10 thin -- and the drift list named neither of his two moved rows. Six further senators and two representatives were hidden by the same arithmetic.
theMeasurementDefectFoundWhileWritingThi.theFix: The pid gate is gone: DRIFT_ROWS is now measured over every pid in the set, set-wise, the way the read-flag check in that same file already was. This is precisely the trap that file's own read-flag note was written about, and the tier list had been left on the wrong side of it. The cost is one extra boot per member.
theMeasurementDefectFoundWhileWritingThi.whyItIsWrittenDownRatherThanQuietlyCorre: A number that moved because the instrument was wrong is the one thing a reader cannot audit from the artifact, and F7's whole claim is that its cost is measured rather than asserted. Runbook rule 21 keeps the first writer's rationale on a live row; the same principle is applied here to a published count.
theMeasurementDefectFoundWhileWritingThi.whatDidNotMove: Nothing in the band table, the row counts, the lane totals or the read-flag check came from the gated list, so no other figure in this disclosure changes: rowsThatStoppedBeingCharacterised was measured over all 343 pids from the start and is still 0.

theShiftThisWaveActuallyCauses.what: 128 of the 184 tier transitions are on restraint, and the two big movements there are 59 members from Split to Mostly supports and 43 from thin to Strongly supports. That is the wave's real published effect and it is named here rather than left inside a net figure.
theShiftThisWaveActuallyCauses.theObjectionAndTheAnswer: The objection is that seven mapped rolls on three texts is repetition, and repetition should not move a reading. The answer is that the direction each senator now reads is the direction that senator actually voted, seven, eight or nine times, and the tier is decided by _RD_DOMINANCE at 0.75 over their own counts -- a floor this wave does not touch. What rule 34 forbids is admitting a duplicate that records nobody's position, and seven rolls were withheld from the mapping table for exactly that reason. What it requires is admitting the roll that is the only record of somebody's position, and three of the four mapped Iran rolls are admitted on precisely that ground: collins, murkowski and cassidy are each recorded voting yea on one roll and nowhere else on that text. Withholding those three would have published a restraint reading for three senators that omits the one time they crossed.
theShiftThisWaveActuallyCauses.whyItIsNotAPartyPattern: No party word appears in any rationale, no party total is mapped, and the crossovers this wave surfaces run in both directions.

readDisclosure.theProceduralLabelOnTheFourteenSenateAct: A DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED BEFORE THE MIGRATION SHIPPED, recorded because the fix is invisible in the final files. The vote seed generator first wrote actionType 'discharge' for the fourteen Senate rolls. vr_rollcalls.action_type is a closed vocabulary and 'discharge' is not in it, so the migration would have filed 'motion' while the seed said something else, and netlify/lib/vr-pack.ts reads exactly two action types as procedural, ['procedural','motion'] -- meaning the reader's own pack would mark these acts procedural and stance-helpers.js would multiply their curator weight by 0.25 before the record index compares the two sides, while every offline harness and every projected measurement read them as substantive at full weight. A four-fold weight difference between the numbers this wave published and the numbers a reader would see. The generator now writes 'motion' and the form-gate record of what was admitted stays in admittedAs and decisiveWhy. WHAT THE CORRECTION MOVED: nothing. The full --set all projection was re-run after the change and the output is byte-identical to the run before it -- same 126 members whose shape moved, same 184 tier transitions, same 31 gained reads, same empty lostReads, same fifteen direction changes. That comparison was then RE-RUN on both sides after the drift instrument itself was corrected (see theMeasurementDefectFoundWhileWritingThis), because an identity proved with a gated measurement proves only that the gate was stable; on the ungated measurement the two runs are still identical, row for row. The reason is that every act a member gains on restraint from this wave carries the same factor, and a uniform scale applied to one side of a lopsided ratio does not cross _RD_DOMINANCE. It is stated as a measurement rather than an argument because the argument would have been wrong in the shape where a member's pre-existing acts on the key run the other way. WHAT IT DOES CHANGE, and the reader sees it: each of these fourteen acts now carries the word procedural on its row, which is true -- a motion to discharge a committee is a procedural question, and the whole reason it is the admitted form here is that no vote on the merits ever followed.
